'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
***[[Tatmadaw]] forces backed by [[Armored car (military)|armoured vehicle]]s and [[artillery]] enter the country's second-largest city [[Mandalay]] and clash with the newly formed [[People's Defence Force (Myanmar)|People's Defence Force]] rebel group which seized parts of the city. Clashes are ongoing. [https://www.msn.com/en-ca/news/world/myanmar-army-fights-anti-junta-militia-in-second-biggest-city-mandalay/ar-AALiEmG (MSN)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***The [[Taliban]] seizes control of [[Shir Khan Bandar]], a town that contains [[Afghanistan]]'s main [[Afghanistan-Tajikistan border|border]] crossing into [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/22/taliban-capture-afghanistans-main-tajikistan-border-crossing (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[South Sudan]] officially resumes the production of [[crude oil]] after a 7-year hiatus. The country's Minister of Petroleum says that production has begun at the [[Block 5A, South Sudan|Block 5A]] oil field and that the country is seeking a production of 8,000 barrels per day. [https://nation.com.pk/22-Jun-2021/south-sudan-oil-block-resumes-production-after-7-years (''The Nation'')]
*Argentine Economy Minister [[Martín Guzmán]] announces that the country will make a voluntary payment to the [[Paris Club]] to avoid default. Argentina is also currently negotiating with the [[International Monetary Fund]]. [https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/economy/argentina-plans-partial-payment-to-paris-club-averting-default.phtml (''Buenos Aires Times'')]
*The [[Japanese government]], in its annual economic policy guidelines, recommends that companies employ a [[four-day workweek]], saying it will improve [[work-life balance]], encourage skill development, and will cause workers to spend more to boost [[Economy of Japan|the economy]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/japan-work-life-balance/a-57989053 (DW)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] receives her second dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. However, Merkel received the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccine for her second dose rather than the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/22/angela-merkel-given-moderna-as-second-covid-19-jab-after-having-astrazeneca-as-first-injec (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
****[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Mario Draghi]] receives his second dose of the [[COVID-19]] [[vaccine]]. However, Draghi received the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine for his second dose instead of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/italy-s-draghi-changes-vaccines-for-second-dose-01624385707 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 546 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of deaths since February 11, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 130,347. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/22/russia-highest-daily-covid-death-toll-since-february (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Turkey]] lowers its [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccination]] eligibility age to 25 as curfews are expected to end this week. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/turkey-lowers-vaccine-eligibility-age-to-25/2281454 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] lifts face mask requirements and capacity restrictions on indoor events. However, masks are still required for nursing homes, prisons, hospitals, schools, funeral directors, and agricultural workers but usage at businesses is optional. [https://www.mlive.com/public-interest/2021/06/michigans-mask-mandates-capacity-limits-are-over-here-are-the-remaining-restrictions.html (MLive.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] reports a record 792 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, and surpasses 90,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.perfil.com/noticias/coronavirus/nuevo-record-muertes-792-covid-argentina-supero-90-mil-fallecidos.phtml (''Perfil'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record 180 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,270. The [[Ministry of Health (Fiji)|Ministry of Health]] also reports two deaths as the disease rapidly spreads across the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445312/180-covid-19-cases-confirmed-in-fiji (RNZ)] [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/world/fiji-records-180-new-covid-19-cases-two-deaths-over-past-24-hours (TVNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***The [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare]] declares the "[[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta Plus]]" [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant of COVID-19]] a Variant of Concern after 22 cases of the variant were reported in [[India]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/delta-plus-variant-of-covid-19-a-variant-of-concern-in-india-govt-101624380173443.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Climate change in Australia]]
**[[UNESCO]] recommends changing the [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage]] status of the [[Great Barrier Reef]] to "[[List of World Heritage in Danger|in danger]]" and urges "accelerated action" from [[Australia]]. Australian [[Minister for the Environment (Australia)|Environment Minister]] [[Sussan Ley]] says that she "strongly opposes" the recommendation, arguing that it was politically motivated and not following normal process. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/22/great-barrier-reef-should-be-listed-as-in-danger-unesco-recommends (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Hungary]], [[LGBT rights in Hungary]]
**A number of European countries, including [[Germany]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Sweden]], [[France]] and [[Ireland]], condemn the recently passed anti-[[LGBT]]Q+ bill in [[Hungary]] which bans the "display and promotion of homosexuality" among under-18s as "grotesque". [[Luxembourg]] says that the bill violates human rights and along with [[Belgium]] says that the bill is a "flagrant form of discrimination". [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/hungarys-new-lgbt-law-contradicts-eu-values-germany-says-2021-06-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]], [[United States–Yemen relations]]
**The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] and [[Bureau of Industry and Security]] seize control of several Iranian websites, including those of [[Press TV]] and [[Al-Alam News Network]], as well as the Houthi-controlled [[Al Masirah TV]]. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/iranian-state-news-sites-appear-seized-us (Voice of America)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
**President [[Rodrigo Duterte]] threatens to arrest those who refuse to be [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines|vaccinated against COVID-19]] and tells them to leave the country if they will not cooperate with efforts to end a public health emergency. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-arrests-health-feeb885f996b2a6f0f425a315c6c5ed9 (AP)]
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The [[Government of Spain|Spanish government]] [[pardon]]s the nine jailed [[Catalan separatist]]s convicted for their roles in the [[Catalan declaration of independence|failed 2017 declaration of independence]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/21/spain-to-approve-pardons-for-9-imprisoned-catalan-separatists-pm-says (Euronews)]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[United Kingdom]] begins testing its new [[Emergency population warning|emergency alert system]] with some [[mobile phone]] users receiving a siren-like sound informing them of the alert test. When the alert service goes live, it will issue warnings to the public about [[terrorism in the United Kingdom|terrorist]] incidents, flooding and public health emergencies. [https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/emergency-alerts-sent-mobile-phones-20871613 (Wales Online)]
